narration: This is Ohafia War Dance. Historical roots, living tradition.

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originates from the Ohafia people of Eastern Nigeria, whose ancestors were known as mighty warriors.
The tradition is linked to the historical practice of beheading fallen enemies as proof of courage, which allowed men to join the Ogbu-Isi society and wear an eagle's plume.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is performed to commemorate the strength of Ohafia ancestors in past wars and to celebrate the achievements of individuals.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by a group of men dressed as warriors.
A lead dancer carries a basket of human skulls (oyaya), a short cutlass, and a palm shoot in his mouth.
The other dancers mime the act of cutting off human heads while moving to the music.
Watch for Miming the cutting of heads.
